edges.description: Ectopic SRY initiates the SOX9-centered testis-determination cascade.
intermediate_mechanisms: SRY transcriptional activity increases SOX9 expression in supporting-cell precursors.

edges.description: Increased SOX9 enhancer dosage activates the testis pathway in an XX gonad.
Ectopic SOX3 activates SOX9 through an SRY-like route.
The Arg92 variant shifts the gonadal regulatory balance toward testis differentiation.
intermediate_mechanisms: Altered NR5A1 target regulation reduces restraint on the male developmental pathway.

edges.description: WT1 C-terminal disruption can redirect 46,XX supporting-cell fate toward testis formation.
Sustained pro-testis signaling directs supporting cells and gonadal architecture toward testes.
Insufficient or asynchronous fetal androgen output can produce atypical external genital anatomy.
Variable fetal androgen effect can include hypospadias.
Abnormal testicular development or descent can result in cryptorchidism.
intermediate_mechanisms: Impaired gonadal development and genital differentiation can disrupt testicular descent.

edges.description: The 46,XX testis lacks the usual Yq AZF complement and progressively loses germ cells.
intermediate_mechanisms: Absence of Yq azoospermia-factor regions impairs germ-cell maintenance and spermatogenesis.

edges.description: Abnormal Sertoli and Leydig compartments can reduce endocrine reserve; the timing and longitudinal progression are not established.
intermediate_mechanisms: Abnormal seminiferous architecture and Leydig-cell dysfunction reduce gonadal feedback and androgen output.

edges.description: Loss of germ cells and AZF-dependent spermatogenesis produces azoospermia.
Germ-cell and seminiferous-tubule loss reduce testicular volume.
Azoospermia prevents biological paternity with autologous sperm in typical non-mosaic disease.
Reduced gonadal feedback raises FSH and LH, with variably low testosterone.
Pubertal/adult gonadal dysfunction can produce gynecomastia.
intermediate_mechanisms: Altered androgen-estrogen balance permits breast tissue development.

nodes.description: Donor-sperm assisted reproductive technology can achieve parenthood for affected couples. The choice among donor insemination, IVF, and other family-building options should be individualized. Autologous sperm retrieval is generally not expected to succeed in confirmed non-mosaic disease lacking AZF regions, but categorical exclusions should be discussed with a reproductive-urology specialist because evidence is limited.

nodes.description: Specific heterozygous substitutions at NR5A1 Arg92 alter the balance between pro-ovary and pro-testis programs. The human association is strong, but the precise transcriptional mechanism remains incompletely resolved.

evidence.reference_title: A recurrent p.Arg92Trp variant in steroidogenic factor-1 (NR5A1) can act as a molecular switch in human sex development.
evidence.snippet: These unique findings highlight how a specific variant in a developmental transcription factor can switch organ fate from the ovary to testis in mammals and represents the first missense mutation causing isolated, non-syndromic 46,XX testicular/ovotesticular DSD in humans.

evidence.reference_title: NR5A1 is a novel disease gene for 46,XX testicular and ovotesticular disorders of sex development.
evidence.snippet: We hypothesize that p.(Arg92Trp) results in decreased inhibition of the male developmental pathway through downregulation of female antitestis genes, thereby tipping the balance toward testicular differentiation in 46,XX individuals.

meta.association: Specific heterozygous Arg92 substitutions are causative; this assertion does not apply to all loss-of-function NR5A1 variants.

evidence.reference_title: A recurrent p.Arg92Trp variant in steroidogenic factor-1 (NR5A1) can act as a molecular switch in human sex development.
evidence.snippet: Here, we show that a specific recurrent heterozygous missense mutation (p.Arg92Trp) in the accessory DNA-binding region of NR5A1 is associated with variable degree of testis development in 46,XX children and adults from four unrelated families.

evidence.reference_title: NR5A1 is a novel disease gene for 46,XX testicular and ovotesticular disorders of sex development.
